description.p: Nordstjernen is a clean-room web browser written from scratch in C, with a GTK 4 user interface and a libcurl network stack. It is built to be small, secure, and readable by a single person end to end.

ul.li: A from-scratch HTML5, CSS, and JavaScript engine — no forked browser engine.
Each tab's engine runs in its own sandboxed process (seccomp + Landlock on Linux) behind an IPC and shared-memory framebuffer boundary.
No JIT, which keeps the JavaScript attack surface small.
WebGL 1/2 enabled by default, with a global setting and visible use indicator.
No telemetry: it does not phone home and does not track the user.
Content-Security-Policy applies per iframe, and response bodies are decoded by the browser, which makes BankID logins work.
The HTTP cache follows RFC 9111, honours stale-while-revalidate and stores private responses; 103 Early Hints are used.
SVG images are drawn sharply at the size they are shown, and SVG text renders in images and backgrounds.
Many layout fixes: percentage heights, inline-block baselines, vertical-align top and bottom, grid track minimums, container queries and the lh unit.
Faster stylesheet parsing and engine start-up.
On Linux the renderer now requires the Landlock filesystem sandbox, and about:nordstjernen reports the sandbox state.
Downloads are fetched by the sandboxed renderer, their file names are sanitised, and they are only moved into Downloads after a path check.
WebAssembly SIMD is supported.
Column flex layout and scrollIntoView fixes, and 1 ms timers on Windows.
Building a long list of elements outside the document is much faster: 20,000 items now take about 30 ms instead of 8 seconds.
Nordstjernen can be installed from npm as nordstjernen-browser.
The Arch Linux package builds the current release.
WebGL canvases that redraw every frame are read back asynchronously and converted on the GPU, so painting is about three times faster and translucent canvases blend correctly.
The browser can be driven remotely over the Model Context Protocol with nordstjernen --mcp.
Many CSS table, flexbox, float, multi-column, fixed positioning and SVG layout fixes, and faster painting of invisible and translucent subtrees.
Security fixes for storage isolation, local file access, web worker requests, FontFace, the clipboard, the MP4 demuxer and renderer-requested downloads.
Alpine and Debian packages carry JPEG XL, H.264/AAC playback, spell-checking and WOFF2 like the other Linux builds.
Google is the default search engine, and the new tab page is redesigned with compact shortcuts and a hint that says whether Enter opens an address or searches.
JavaScript gains Temporal, ShadowRealm, decorators, deferred module imports, Intl.Segmenter and the rest of Intl inside the engine, and WHATWG Streams.
CSS gains anchor positioning, scroll-driven animations, the shape() function, size containment, mask-border and Color 4/5 parsing.
Videos are composited as their own window layer for smoother playback, and H.264/AAC are decoded by the operating system.
Adding a stylesheet or changing the DOM restyles only the elements it can affect.
Many layout fixes for tables, grids, inline boxes and line heights, and security fixes in select, regular expressions, module loading and WebGL 2.
Pages receive wheel events and can cancel scrolling, and pointer releases report where the button was let go, so maps zoom and pan as expected.
XPath 1.0 is implemented through document.evaluate and XPathResult.
Web Audio plays sound, YouTube videos no longer skip or stutter, and Ogg Theora video plays inline.
WebGPU is on by default, like WebGL, and Google Maps draws its map on NVIDIA graphics.
Inline SVG foreignObject renders its HTML content, and many layout fixes for absolutely positioned, flex and scrolled boxes.
Restyling, relayout and stylesheet handling are faster on pages with many styles.
Security fixes: web pages can no longer read local files, change settings or wipe browsing data, and WebGL, WebGPU and Web Audio no longer touch freed memory.

WebGPU is part of every desktop build and can be switched on in Settings; it gains render bundles, error scopes, every texture format, full pipeline state and subgroups, and page mistakes no longer crash the renderer.
WebGL offers compressed textures and the common extensions, and fixes black environment-lit scenes, invisible particles and multi-view canvases.
WebAssembly runs on a much faster interpreter and works from several workers at once, so Draco, Basis and IFC models in three.js load in seconds.
WebGL and WebGPU canvases can be saved with toDataURL and toBlob.
Restyling after DOM changes is much faster, and scripts and JavaScript modules load in parallel.
Form controls, inline boxes, shadows and fonts look and measure as in Chrome; Reddit, Yahoo, Netflix and Twitch render correctly.
JPEG XL images are displayed.

description.p: Sharp HiDPI rendering, smooth scrolling, layout and security release.

ul.li: Pages are drawn at the screen's real pixel density, so text and images are sharp on Retina and other HiDPI displays.
Scrolling is smooth and no longer waits for the page's scripts: the window moves pre-painted tiles itself, with touchpad momentum and eased wheel and key scrolling.
Clipboard in text fields: paste with Ctrl+V and a new right-click menu with Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All.
Text flows around floats, margins collapse and flex, grid and line heights are sized as in other browsers, fixing layout on Wikipedia, GitHub, MDN, apple.com and Stack Overflow.
Text uses the same fonts and widths as Chrome on macOS, and WOFF2 and variable web fonts load correctly.
Signing in to Google and opening Gmail works.
A security audit fixed many memory-safety bugs reachable from web content and tightened the sandbox and web security policy.
Restyles, relayouts, event dispatch and box shadows are much faster; the experimental V8 backend is removed.

description.p: Dual licensing, performance and compatibility release.

ul.li: Nordstjernen is dual-licensed under the Nordstjernen Source License v1.0 or the GNU GPL version 3 or later.
Style resolution, script parsing, form access and container-query relayout are faster; Speedometer's Complex-DOM suites run about 18% faster.
Constructed style sheets adopted by shadow roots work again, and pages with many shadow roots no longer crash the renderer.
instanceof follows the prototype chain, so Vue apps render HTML elements correctly.
YouTube video events fire once per resource, ads no longer leave the player stalled, and forced layouts on the watch page are much faster.
The built-in pages and the browser window have a new, flatter look with light and dark colours.

description.p: Frames, events, workers and robustness release.

ul.li: Frames behave as in other browsers: each has its own document lifecycle, WindowProxy, event handlers and performance timeline, and postMessage and MessagePort work across frames.
Events, structured cloning, dedicated workers and focus handling follow the HTML standard more closely, and scripts written by document.write or inserted with append() run.
Deeply nested pages, SVGs and CSS values no longer crash the renderer.
The desktop browser records visited pages in History again, and YouTube and other MSE players play video again.
align-content works on block containers, and textareas honour CSS heights and keep their placeholder while focused.
Nordstjernen can also be built on Fabrice Bellard's original QuickJS, and builds against GLib 2.90.

description.p: Grid, dialogs, security and styling performance release.

ul.li: CSS Grid runs the full track-sizing algorithm for every grid, including grid-template-areas layouts, grids beyond 24 rows and fr rows that fill a container's height; the grid shorthands parse and serialize per their grammars.
Popovers, dialog and light dismiss follow the HTML standard, :focus-visible is matched separately from :focus, and the autofocus attribute works.
Cross-origin frames and images are isolated: an embedding page can no longer read or script another site's frame, cookies or image pixels, and the audio helper only opens media a page may play.
Styling large pages is much faster: rules are indexed instead of tried on every element, style sharing is corrected and relayouts no longer re-scan every style sheet.

The default stylesheet follows the HTML rendering section, legacy presentational attributes and quirks mode are honoured, and tables, floats, flexbox and multi-column layout follow the specifications more closely.
The Android app is about 8 MB smaller.

description.p: Animations, CSS validation and interface release.

ul.li: Transitions and animations run for every property; the Web Animations surface (document.getAnimations(), Animation objects, keyframe effects) and animation and transition events by phase follow the specifications, and several CSS animations run on one element.

Container queries evaluate the full condition grammar, and image-set(), transform, the background and border shorthands, aspect-ratio, box-shadow, attr() and percentage border radii are validated and serialized per their CSS grammars.

Tables measure min-content and max-content widths column by column, position: fixed boxes stay anchored to the viewport, and rtl static positions and single-choice select defaults follow the specifications.
The toolbar takes the classic look of the Northstar web browser, with labelled colour buttons for Back, Forward, Reload, Stop, Home, Print and Downloads.
Fullscreen is announced with a notice naming the site, needs a user gesture, and ends on navigation, tab switch and tab close.
about:start wears the Northstar splash, an xkcd-style comic of Noah's ark, retitled for Nordstjernen.
quickjs-ng updated to v0.16.2; the .deb no longer bundles the dynamic loader.

description.p: Layout, CSS and forms compliance release.

ul.li: Flex layout resolves flexible lengths as css-flexbox-1 §9.7 describes, column containers wrap, and negative free space overflows in the right direction; WPT css-flexbox rises from 1465 to 1997 passing subtests.

Grid: rtl columns, repeat(auto-fit) track collapsing, grid-placed containing blocks for absolutely positioned boxes, resolved track sizes in getComputedStyle, and em, calc() and fr tracks sized per the specification.

CSS parsing: gradients, the font shorthand, font-family lists, the content property and alignment keywords are validated against their grammars and serialize canonically; a parser hang on at-rules inside declaration lists is fixed.
Forms follow the HTML constraint-validation specification for ValidityState and pattern, stepUp() and stepDown() follow the stepping algorithm, showPicker() exists, and control.labels is live.
Live collections, moveBefore(), replaceChildren() and isConnected follow the DOM specification; document.fonts.ready waits for web fonts.

The user decides what runs: an Enable JavaScript switch in Settings, popup blocking gated on user activation, view-source: with Ctrl+U, Ctrl+D bookmarking, Ctrl+Enter address completion and a cache-bypassing hard reload.
Fixed use-after-free bugs in the MutationObserver drain, in callbacks that navigate, and in Web Audio and canvas paths that read page-owned ArrayBuffers.
A new impressionist about:start splash.

The browser prints: Ctrl+P lays the page out for paper and hands the sheets to the operating system's own print dialog, with @media print, @page and the break-before/after/inside properties deciding where a sheet ends.

Layout: offsetLeft and offsetTop are measured from the offsetParent, absolutely positioned flex children take their static position from the flexbox algorithm, and flex-wrap: wrap-reverse turns the cross axis around.
CSS Scroll Snap moves a scroll container onto the nearest snap position, honouring scroll-padding and scroll-margin.

Two paragraphs measuring the same words come out the same width, processing instructions are parsed as processing instructions, and a regular expression whose v-flag class contains the empty string compiles.

Distribution packaging builds from a release tarball again: the FFmpeg dependency is declared, a source RPM carries a version rpm accepts, the Debian tree has the changelog dpkg-buildpackage needs, and a build host without network reaches the system copies.
The Android, iOS and Java hosts compile again, and the NetBSD build installs its dependencies from the CDN rather than a single mirror.
Text is shaped through ns-pango, a fork of Pango that caches finished glyph strings and font metrics process-wide, so the same words are shaped once rather than once per measurement.

Interface: the toolbar menu is grouped into tab, view, page and tool sections, the page zoom and bookmark state show beside the address bar, the status line only appears when it has something to say, and Escape reverts the address bar to the URL on screen.

Layout: grid items placed by area name are aligned, a single flex line fills its container, percentages inside min(), max() and clamp() resolve, grid tracks take any length unit, and inline-block boxes sit on the line's baseline.

Web platform: worker scopes get the same JavaScript platform the page does, event listeners follow the Web IDL callback-interface algorithm, document.styleSheets lists linked sheets, and OfflineAudioContext renders audio.
The Android shell gained forward history, find-in-page, sharing and pull-to-refresh, and re-lays out the open document on rotation rather than refetching it.
The Java binding builds with Maven and speaks the whole renderer control protocol, and the Swing browser uses it.
SVG renders in the engine: gradients, masks, markers, patterns, text and var() in presentation attributes, with librsvg dropped entirely.
Images decode only in-tree — ICO, Wuffs, libwebp, libavif, SVG — so gdk-pixbuf loader plugins no longer parse untrusted bytes.
Media: HLS and DASH play over Media Source Extensions, animated PNG and animated WebP animate, and the WebRTC and media-capture object surface is complete.
CSS: cascade layers order as a tree, Media Queries Level 4 evaluation, border-image, container units, and a much more complete CSSOM.
Layout: flex sizing follows the flex algorithm, anonymous table boxes are generated for every table-internal display, and nested flex rows no longer lay out in exponential time.
Networking: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 client fixes, subresource fetch de-duplication, and Vary-aware cache variant selection.

description.p: Email client, media, and rendering release.

ul.li: Built-in email (about:email): IMAP/POP3/SMTP with one-step provider setup for Gmail, Yahoo, iCloud and Fastmail, app-password and 2-step-verification guidance, and attachment viewing.
An optional primary password encrypts saved mail credentials at rest with PBKDF2-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM.
Media: initial Media Source Extensions (MSE) append path.
Rendering: replaced elements (img, video, canvas, svg) are sized per the CSS rendering spec and default to inline-level.
Networking: per-host concurrent-fetch cap and tighter media/renderer IPC bounds.

description.p: Extensions, content blocking, and engine hardening release.

ul.li: Initial WebExtensions support with declarativeNetRequest content blocking and EasyList/ABP filter lists.
Local SafeBrowsing-style phishing and malware protection.
Updated vendored QuickJS and Lexbor engines, with DOM, XHR, and CSS spec-compliance fixes.
Shared curl multi handle with HTTP/2 connection multiplexing and reuse.
Tabbed Developer Tools window expanding the JavaScript console.
Net Center masthead refresh and sign-in button layout fixes.
Inline atomic box layout positioning correction.
New audio path: SDL2 output with in-tree pl_mpeg (MP2) and minimp3 (MP3) decoding, replacing the vendored miniaudio backend.
Security hardening: bounded EventSource reconnect delay, a fixed image-source memory leak, and a tightened renderer IPC reply limit.
